digest.component_or_area: tickets repository maintenance and epoch enforcement
propositions: A one-time force-push rewrite of the tickets repository branch must execute only after all precursor tasks (A1-A5, A6-0a through A6-0d, and Epic B's B6) are closed and zero active sessions and rebar-mcp servers are confirmed stopped by operator attestation.

The epoch guard mechanism replaces the prior 24-hour fixed precondition; correctness is proven by direct runtime evidence (deployed review-bot refusal probe, explicitly refreshed host binary epoch-mismatch probe, and completed descendant reconcile-bridge run ancestry) rather than elapsed time.

Repository state is verified before and after the force-push via pre-rewrite clone assertions (tree equality, commit/merge-commit count stability, size < 150 MiB), identity verification summary deduplication, old-tip non-resurrection checks, and fsck cleanness to prevent data loss or resurrection of deleted commits.

The landed rebar.toml identity.enforce_since value must equal the mapped post-rewrite SHA, verified after the first deterministic post-window write (review-bot LLM-Review vote on the enforce_since re-pin change).

Post-window reconciliation (reconcile-bridge.yml and canary runs) must exit cleanly with zero Jira mutation failures and zero drift, and the signed CLI substitute (if GitHub Actions is unavailable) must provide equivalent signed proof of state convergence.

All 12 acceptance criteria must pass under operator attestation and code-verifiable gates before publication is considered complete; force-close bypasses only automated verification, not the substantive checks themselves.
